note.question: How should an ad network coordinate publisher payments and fraud-detection strictness, and can removing malicious publishers backfire?
note.overview: An ad network moves first in payment and fraud-detection configuration, publishers respond in participation and fraud generation, and advertisers update valuation; equilibrium is solved by backward induction.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The ad network first chooses publisher payments and detection sensitivities. Publishers then decide participation and, if malicious, fraud quantity. Valid and charged traffic are realized; advertisers update per-unit valuation from campaign performance, and payoffs follow. Payments are an economic lever while sensitivity is a technological lever.

components.label: Backward-induction equilibrium of the three-stage ad-network game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Backward-induction equilibrium of the three-stage ad-network game. Section 3.5, printed pp. 10-11 (PDF pp. 10-11), states the three-stage sequence. Section 4 explicitly solves the game by backward induction, and Lemma 1 on printed pp. 11-12 (PDF pp. 11-12) characterizes equilibrium payments and configurations; the paper does not label the solution concept subgame-perfect equilibrium.
